summary: A fiduciary or specialist, working for an estate, law firm, trust company or as a named digital executor, who inventories a deceased or incapacitated person's online accounts, devices, crypto and data, then gains lawful access, preserves, transfers, memorializes or deletes them under laws like RUFADAA and platform tools like Apple Legacy Contact and Google Inactive Account Manager. AI helps most with inventory triage, platform-procedure research, access-request letters, family communication and planning documents, while the human keeps legal authority and never handles live credentials or private content through the AI.

prompts.title: Digital asset inventory triage
prompts.task: Turn scattered clues into a structured inventory of accounts and assets
prompts.prompt: You are assisting a digital estate executor. From the redacted clues below (email subject lines, bank statement merchant names, app list, browser bookmarks), build an inventory table with columns: Asset/service, Category (financial, crypto, communications, social, cloud storage, subscription, domain/IP, loyalty points), Evidence source, Likely value (monetary/sentimental/none), Recurring charge?, Access route (platform legacy tool, RUFADAA request, password manager, unknown), Priority (urgent/normal/low). Flag items suggesting self-custodied crypto or business accounts. Then list accounts that commonly exist but have no evidence yet, as questions for the family. Jurisdiction: [STATE/COUNTRY]. Clues: [PASTE REDACTED CLUES - NO PASSWORDS OR SEED PHRASES].
prompts.caution: Never paste passwords, seed phrases, recovery codes or full account numbers into an AI chat.

prompts.title: Platform access procedure lookup
prompts.task: Map the right request path for each major platform
prompts.prompt: I am the [EXECUTOR/ADMINISTRATOR/TRUSTEE/AGENT UNDER POA] for [DECEDENT OR INCAPACITATED PERSON] in [JURISDICTION]. For each platform listed, summarize: whether a user-designated tool exists (e.g. Apple Legacy Contact, Google Inactive Account Manager, Facebook legacy contact), whether that tool was likely set up given [WHAT WE KNOW], what the platform typically requires otherwise (death certificate, letters testamentary, court order), whether it grants content access or only memorialization/closure, and realistic timelines. Present as a table, then note where your information may be out of date so I verify on the platform's current help pages. Platforms: [LIST].
prompts.caution: Platform policies change often; confirm every procedure on the platform's official help center before filing.

prompts.title: RUFADAA access request letter
prompts.task: Draft a custodian request for catalogue or content disclosure
prompts.prompt: Draft a request letter from a fiduciary to [CUSTODIAN, e.g. email provider] under [STATE]'s enactment of the Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act. Fiduciary type: [PERSONAL REPRESENTATIVE/TRUSTEE/AGENT/CONSERVATOR]. Requested scope: [CATALOGUE OF COMMUNICATIONS ONLY / CONTENT / CLOSURE]. Basis for content access: [WILL PROVISION OR USER CONSENT, OR NONE KNOWN]. Include the enclosures RUFADAA typically requires, a clear account identifier field, a preservation request, and a polite response deadline. After the letter, list which statute sections I should cite and have my attorney verify, and explain the catalogue-vs-content distinction and how the Stored Communications Act affects it.
prompts.caution: Not legal advice; have estate counsel review, especially for content requests and non-US custodians.

prompts.title: Crypto and self-custody risk plan
prompts.task: Plan safe recovery of crypto holdings without exposing keys
prompts.prompt: You are advising a digital estate executor on crypto assets. Known facts: [EXCHANGES USED, HARDWARE WALLET MODELS FOUND, NOTES ABOUT SEED STORAGE - NO ACTUAL SEEDS]. Produce a step-by-step plan covering: exchange account claims (what estates usually submit), handling hardware wallets and seed backups (chain of custody, two-person rule, air-gapped device, never entering seeds online), recognizing scam 'recovery services', valuation at date of death for tax purposes in [JURISDICTION], and when to bring in a forensic specialist. End with a checklist of decisions requiring beneficiary or court sign-off.
prompts.caution: Never share seed phrases or private keys with any AI or third party; one leak means irreversible loss.

prompts.title: Family update and sensitive-content policy
prompts.task: Explain the process and decisions to grieving heirs
prompts.prompt: Write a compassionate, plain-language update email from me, the digital estate executor, to [FAMILY MEMBERS] about [DECEDENT]'s online accounts. Cover: what has been found so far [SUMMARY], what will be memorialized, closed or preserved per [WILL/DIGITAL ASSET DIRECTIVE OR 'NO INSTRUCTIONS'], expected timelines, and a decision they need to make about [e.g. keeping the Facebook profile memorialized]. Address respectfully that private messages may not be read by anyone unless authorized and why. Keep under 350 words, warm but precise, no legal jargon. Also give a two-sentence version suitable for a text message.
prompts.caution: Respect the decedent's privacy choices; do not promise access the law or platforms may not grant.

prompts.title: Digital estate plan for a living client
prompts.task: Draft a pre-need digital asset directive and setup checklist
prompts.prompt: Help me prepare a digital estate plan for a living client, [AGE/SITUATION], in [JURISDICTION]. Produce: (1) a checklist of platform-level settings to configure now (Apple Legacy Contact, Google Inactive Account Manager, Facebook legacy contact, password manager emergency access such as 1Password or Bitwarden), (2) draft clauses for their attorney to adapt granting a fiduciary access to digital assets and electronic communication content, (3) a template inventory sheet that references where credentials are stored rather than containing them, (4) wishes to record (delete, archive, memorialize). Flag points that depend on local law, e.g. outside the US.
prompts.caution: Clauses are drafts for a licensed attorney; online tool designations can override wills under RUFADAA.

prompts.title: Cross-border and data-protection issues
prompts.task: Spot jurisdictional conflicts for an international estate
prompts.prompt: The decedent lived in [COUNTRY], held accounts with providers based in [COUNTRIES], and heirs are in [COUNTRIES]. As a research aid for a digital estate executor, outline: which law likely governs fiduciary access, how GDPR treats deceased persons' data (Recital 27) and examples of member states with their own rules (e.g. France's post-mortem data directives), relevant court precedents such as Germany's 2018 Facebook inheritance ruling, and US provider obligations under the Stored Communications Act. Present as an issues list with 'settled', 'contested' and 'unknown' tags, and the questions I should put to local counsel in each country.
prompts.caution: This area is unsettled and fast-changing; treat output as a research starting point, not a legal opinion.

prompts.title: Upskilling study plan
prompts.task: Build a learning path for the role
prompts.prompt: I am a [CURRENT ROLE, e.g. paralegal / IT support / estate planner] moving into digital estate administration. Create a 12-week study plan covering: RUFADAA and probate basics in [JURISDICTION], the Stored Communications Act and CFAA (why logging in with a decedent's password can be risky), major platform legacy policies, password manager and device forensics basics, crypto custody and estate tax valuation, grief-informed communication, and data protection. For each week give objectives, one primary source to read (statute text, official platform help pages, Uniform Law Commission materials), and a practical exercise. Note relevant credentials or associations if any exist and say plainly where none do.
